cards.text: Jesus is wrapping up a long teaching for His disciples on the Mount of Olives (Matthew 24:3), and He saves this one for last. When the Son of Man, the name Jesus uses for Himself (Matthew 8:20), comes in His glory with ALL the angels, He will sit on His glorious throne. And everything that follows happens in front of that throne.

cards.question: When the Son of Man is seated on His glorious throne, who is gathered before Him?

cards.text: Then Jesus says, "He will separate the people one from another, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats." Now THAT is a sort, friend. I tried sorting my sprinkles by color once. Two hours later? One jar. Rainbow. AGAIN.

cards.question: The Son of Man will place the sheep on His ___ and the goats on His ___.

cards.text: Now Jesus calls Him the King, and the King speaks to the ones on His right. His first word to them is "Come," and after years in the back of a junk drawer, friend, that word would've had me hopping, gold base and all.

cards.question: The King tells the ones on His right, who are blessed by His Father, to inherit something. What is it?
The King says this kingdom was put together for them at the last minute.

cards.text: Then the King tells them why: when He was hungry, they gave Him something to eat, when He was thirsty, they gave Him something to drink, and when He was a stranger, they took Him in.

cards.question: Hungry, thirsty, a stranger. What do all the moments on the King's list have in common so far?

answers.text: He was in need and they helped
He was honored and they bowed
He was teaching and they listened

cards.question: The King also says that when He was sick they looked after Him, and when He was in prison they visited Him.

cards.text: Then the righteous, the ones on the King's right, answer Him. And friend, they've got a question for Him.

cards.question: The righteous go down the King's list: hungry, thirsty, a stranger, naked, sick, in prison. What do they keep asking Him?

answers.text: When they ever saw Him that way
Why He never told them sooner
How He made it through all that

cards.question: The King answers the righteous. What does He say about whatever they did for one of the least of these brothers of His?

cards.text: Then the King turns to the ones on His left, and this part is heavy, friend. Instead of "Come," He says, "Depart from Me, you who are cursed, into the eternal fire".

cards.question: The King says the eternal fire was prepared for someone. Who is it?

cards.text: Then the King gives the reason, and it's that list again. When He was hungry, they gave Him nothing to eat, and when He was thirsty, they gave Him nothing to drink.

cards.question: The King says the ones on His left did cruel things to Him when He was a stranger, naked, sick and in prison.
Just like the righteous, the ones on the King's left ask Him when they ever saw Him in need.
The King answers the ones on His left. What does He say about whatever they did not do for one of the least of these?

answers.text: They did not do it for Him
It was too small to count

cards.text: And this is where Jesus lands it. The ones on the left go away into eternal punishment.

cards.question: The ones on the left go away into eternal punishment. Where does Jesus say the righteous go?

findings.problem: The quoted sentence is followed by six more sentences or standalone fragments, so this story card far exceeds the two-sentence limit.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The setup only says that the people will be separated as sheep and goats. Nothing earlier lets the baker reason out their placement, so the blanks simply ask for the unseen wording of verse 33: right and left.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
